To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the mobile workers in this study were highly mobile, with 50% of their time being spent outside of the office; (b) mobile workers were able to use mobile technologies to access remote people and information anytime, anywhere; (c) the use of mobile technologies was not always successful and was often constrained by factors such as the availability of wireless networks and the need to use a desktop PC to access information; (d) mobile workers had to plan their use of mobile technologies to

mobile workers are not always mobile; that they use their mobile technologies in a variety of ways, some of which are surprising, and that they do so in a variety of places; that they do not necessarily use their mobile technologies to work anywhere, anytime; and that their use of these technologies is influenced by a number of factors that are not always obvious.
mobile workers need to plan their activities, to work in "dead time" and to monitor the activities of remote co-workers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which mobile work is changing and how it is supported by technology and artifacts.
the role of technology in the work of mobile workers.
the design of technology to support mobile workers, and the study of how technology is used by mobile workers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mobility is not just about being on the move, it is a complex phenomenon that involves many factors and issues that are not necessarily directly linked to technology.
the use of mobile technologies is not simply a matter of providing people with access to remote resources anytime, anywhere.
mobile workers need to be able to access information and people anytime and anywhere, and they need to be able, in turn, to be monitored by their colleagues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are moving from the office to the network, but we still need to be in touch with the people we work with.
the use of mobile devices and applications in the workplace is still in its infancy, and there are still many opportunities for further development and innovation in this area.
we are not yet able to support mobile work as it happens in practice and that there are many issues to be considered when designing systems for supporting mobile work.
The main takeaway from our work is that

mobile work is more complex and nuanced than the "access anywhere anytime" mantra would suggest, and that it is important to take into account the different facets of access in the design of technological artifacts.
mobile workers do not always work anywhere, anytime.
mobility is not simply about access to information and resources anytime and anywhere.
